subject: Invitation & apostille logistics for Johannesburg workshop
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Thabo Mokoena <thabo@capevisa.co.za>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Invitation & apostille logistics for Johannesburg workshop

Hi Thabo,

We’ve locked in the MediCorps executive workshop in Johannesburg for the week of Dec 8–10. I need your help to get two of our U.S. employees (names below) through the visa process ASAP so they can travel on Dec 7 evening.

Attendees who need paperwork:
- Nina Patel – Sr Product (MediCorps contact) – will be the host on the invitation
- Mark Voss – Redwood engineer (traveling)
- Claire D. – Redwood account lead (traveling)

What we need from your side:
1) A formal invitation letter on MediCorps letterhead that states the purpose (executive workshop), dates (Dec 8–10), and that costs are covered by MediCorps. The letter should include the full passport names and passport numbers.
2) Guidance on apostille/attestation: our passports and a previously notarized CVs are U.S.-issued and may need an apostille from the Secretary of State. Confirm whether South Africa requires apostille or embassy attestation for U.S. documents for these short business visas.
3) Embassy appointment options (any weekend/after-hours fasttrack slots) or a reliable courier that can do a visa drop-off and pickup. If you can secure a guaranteed slot with confirmation/reference number, we’ll pay the premium.
4) A draft invite attached to the HubSpot deal so Ben/Marcus can redline. Please send the draft as PDF and an editable Word doc if possible.

Passport copies and DP for Mark and Claire are attached to this thread. We’ll need the final invitation and an apostille checklist by Dec 2 latest to make the courier cutoff.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive.

Best,
Irene

Attachments: passport-copy-IRN.pdf (two passport images, redacted)
From: Thabo Mokoena <thabo@capevisa.co.za>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Invitation & apostille logistics for Johannesburg workshop

Hi Irene (and team),

Thanks — happy to help. Quick summary and next steps from our side:

1) Invitation letter: I’ve prepared a draft (attached ZA-invite-draft.pdf). It follows the standard embassy wording: host details, dates, and confirmation of cost coverage. I can convert to Word if you need to edit directly.

2) Apostille vs. attestation: For short-term business visas South Africa typically accepts U.S.-notarized documents with an apostille. In rare cases (if the embassy requests) an additional consular legalization is asked, but that’s uncommon for the category you’ve described. So plan for: notary -> Secretary of State apostille. If you tell me the U.S. state the notary is in, I can confirm exact turn times.

3) Embassy slots / courier: The South African Embassy in DC is offering a limited weekend fast-track via a third-party courier we work with — they guarantee a 48–72h turnaround (premium). Courier details and rates attached (courier-rate-sheet.pdf). If you want us to book, we need the finalized invite + apostilled docs by COB Dec 1.

4) Required docs list (what you should send back to me):
- Scanned passport bio pages (clear)
- Signed letter of invitation (editable preferred)
- Notarized CVs (if required by employer) – best to apostille the signed notary pages
- Completed visa application form (we’ll send link)

I’ve penciled in a tentative courier slot for Dec 3 pickup pending your confirmation. If you prefer direct embassy appointment, I can try for Dec 4 morning but availability is not guaranteed.

I attached ZA-invite-draft.pdf and courier-rate-sheet.pdf.

Regards,
Thabo
CapeVisa Services
Attachments: ZA-invite-draft.pdf, courier-rate-sheet.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Invitation & apostille logistics for Johannesburg workshop

Irene — quick edits below after review of the draft. Marcus, please confirm the passport numbers before I send final to Thabo.

Edits to draft (high level):
- Add full job titles for Mark and Claire and include their US work addresses on the invite to match embassy preferences.
- Remove the sentence promising coverage of all incidentals (keep travel + accommodation only).
- Add a line asking for letter to state explicitly that MediCorps will host the workshop and is not hiring or contracting the visitors.

Timing: I can sign off by EOD today if Marcus confirms passport numbers. Once we have the signed invite, Thabo has offered the Dec 3 courier pickup / 48–72h service. That meets our timeline but is tight.

Deal: RWI-5742 — I updated the HubSpot record with the draft (link in metadata).

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
